strongest_angle: Analyzing the Harvard Program on Negotiation framework regarding how top negotiators balance value creation and value claiming to expand the pie.

key_facts.fact: According to the Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School, integrative bargaining is a negotiation strategy focused on uncovering shared and differing interests to create value for both sides rather than simply dividing a fixed pie.
key_facts.source_name: Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School

key_facts.fact: Author Charles B. Craver published an article in the Cardozo Journal of Conflict Resolution titled Value Creation and Value Claiming discussing the inherent tension present in commercial negotiations.
Katie Shonk wrote in a Program on Negotiation article that effective business negotiators know how to collaborate and compete at the same time by balancing value creation and value claiming.
key_facts.source_name: Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School

key_facts.fact: Chapter 3 of the negotiation strategy text outlines that the first three steps are important for creating value while the fourth step involves claiming value.
